title: Suosittelisin toista korjaamoa
subtitle: I would recommend a different repair shop

blocks.text: You already own suosittelen (I recommend, Lesson 1) and oli (was, Lesson 2). This lesson softens both of them into 'would' — the conditional mood. It's the sound of hindsight in these reviews: what should have happened, what a reviewer would do differently. It shows up constantly in the angriest complaints, right where the reviewer stops reporting and starts advising.

blocks.translation: I would recommend a different repair shop.

blocks.title: Conditional as controlled anger
blocks.text: When Finnish reviewers get truly frustrated, they don't raise their voice in the grammar — they shift into conditional. 'Olisi pitänyt vain puhdistaa jarrupalat' (they should have just cleaned the brake pads) reads calmer than a flat accusation, but it lands harder, because it quietly states exactly what competent work would have looked like.

blocks.content: From Lesson 1, suosittelen is 'I recommend'. Slide {-isi-|grammar|conditional infix|would} in before the personal ending and you get suosittelisin — 'I would recommend'. That's the entire trick: find the verb stem, insert -isi-, then add back the person ending you already know (-n for 'I').

items.en: I would recommend a different repair shop.

items.fi: En {suosittelisi|grammar|conditional negative|would not recommend} tätä paikkaa.
items.en: I would not recommend this place.

blocks.content: You know on → oli (is → was) from Lesson 2. The same verb has a conditional too: {olisi|grammar|conditional of 'on'|would be}. Paired with pitänyt (a past participle meaning 'had to/ought'), olisi pitänyt is one of the most common phrases in complaint reviews — 'should have'.

items.fi: {Olisi|grammar|conditional of 'on'|would be} pitänyt vain puhdistaa jarrupalat.
items.en: They should have just cleaned the brake pads.
The price would have been the same.

blocks.title: Same -isi- trick, one more verb
blocks.text: From Lesson 2, kannattaa means 'it's worth it'. Its conditional, {kannattaisi|grammar|conditional|it would be worth it}, softens blunt advice into a gentler suggestion — the difference between 'do this' and 'you might want to do this'.

items.fi: {Kannattaisi|grammar|conditional|it would be worth it} pyytää tarjous kirjallisena.
items.en: It would be worth asking for a written quote.

items.fi: {Kannattaisi|grammar|conditional|it would be worth it} kiinnittää huomiota hintaan.
items.en: It would be worth paying attention to the price.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Would you recommend this repair shop?

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: No. I'd recommend a different repair shop.

lines.speaker: B
lines.fi: Olisi pitänyt vaihtaa vain yksi osa, mutta veloitettiin monesta.
lines.en: Only one part should have been changed, but I was charged for several.

blocks.title: Paul Noble Rule
blocks.text: Every conditional in this lesson is built from a verb you already own: suosittelen, on, kannattaa. That's the whole point of -isi- — it's not a new vocabulary list, it's a lens you place over words you already have. Once the lens clicks, you can turn almost any verb from Lessons 1 to 4 into its 'would' version yourself.

blocks.content: Suosittelisin: SUO-sit-te-li-sin (five syllables — slow down through the middle, the -isi- is the part learners rush). Olisi: O-li-si (short, even, stress on O). Kannattaisi: KAN-nat-tai-si (the 'ai' glides like English 'eye').

rows.en: it would be worth it (conditional of kannattaa)

blocks.title: What you now own
items: suosittelisin / en suosittelisi — I would / wouldn't recommend
olisi pitänyt — should have (the classic hindsight complaint)
kannattaisi — it would be worth it (softer than kannattaa)
the -isi- pattern itself, ready to apply to other verbs you already know
You can now read the calm, controlled tone of Finnish hindsight complaints
You can turn any 'I recommend' style sentence into a polite 'I would recommend'
